# Automate meeting note‑taking with Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams

> **In short:** In a Microsoft Teams meeting, Copilot can answer questions about what has been said, and after the meeting you can reopen it from the meeting chat's Recap tab. For Copilot to help after the meeting ends, live transcription must be turned on during the meeting. You need a work license that includes it.

Taking notes while you also try to listen is hard. With Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams, you can ask for a quick summary, open questions, or a list of ideas while the meeting is still going, and come back to the same Copilot conversation later. This guide follows Microsoft's own support pages.

## Before you start

- **The right license.** Microsoft's support page says intelligent recap is available as part of the Microsoft 365 Copilot license, and also in Teams Premium, an add-on license. Ask your IT admin if you're not sure what you have.
- **A meeting inside your organization.** Microsoft says Copilot won't work in meetings hosted outside the participant's organization.
- **Permission to transcribe.** Let people know before you start; Teams also shows everyone a notification.
- **About 10 minutes** to try it in a short test meeting.

## Step 1: Turn on live transcription

In the meeting, select **More actions** in the meeting controls, then select **Transcribe**. Confirm the language everyone is speaking and select **Confirm**. Microsoft's support page says all participants see a notification that the meeting is being transcribed.

Why this matters: Copilot can be turned on without transcription, but Microsoft says you need live transcription during the meeting to ask Copilot about the meeting or see your Copilot conversation after it ends. Depending on the meeting options, selecting Copilot may also ask you to start transcription.

You'll know it worked when the transcription notification appears and the spoken text starts showing with speaker names and time stamps.

## Step 2: Ask Copilot during the meeting

Select **Copilot** in the meeting controls. This opens a private chat with Copilot that other attendees don't see. Type a question about the meeting so far.

💬 Example: "List the ideas discussed so far, including people's feedback."

Other prompts from Microsoft's support page include "Where do we disagree on this topic?" and "What questions can I ask to move the meeting forward?" If you join more than 5 minutes late and Copilot is active, Teams sends a notification, and you can select **Open Copilot** for a catch-up summary.

You'll know it worked when Copilot answers in the side panel based on what has been said.

## Step 3: Find the recap after the meeting

Go to **Chat** and open the chat of the past meeting. Select **Recap**. If transcription was on, you can open Copilot there and see the same conversation history you had during the meeting. You can also select **Open Copilot** in the upper-right corner of the meeting chat. The full transcript is under **Recap** › **Transcript**, where you can download it.

💬 Example: "Summarize the decisions and the next steps, and say who agreed to do what."

You'll know it worked when your earlier Copilot conversation appears and Copilot answers new questions about the finished meeting.

## Step 4: Turn the notes into a document

For longer answers, Microsoft says you can select **Open in Word**, and for tables, **Open in Excel**. From there you can tidy up the notes and share them the usual way, for example by attaching the file to an email. Read the notes first and correct anything Copilot got wrong before you send them to others.

💬 Example: "Create a table with the action items, the owner, and the due date mentioned in the meeting."

You'll know it worked when the notes open in Word or Excel and you can edit them.

## Common mistakes

- **Forgetting transcription.** Without it, Copilot isn't available about the meeting after it ends. *The fix:* Start transcription at the beginning of the meeting (Step 1).
- **Trying it in a meeting hosted by another organization.** Microsoft says Copilot won't work there. *The fix:* Use it in meetings inside your own organization.
- **Sending notes without reading them.** Copilot can misunderstand who said what. *The fix:* Check the summary against the transcript before you share it.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** If you lead a volunteer group or a club that meets in Teams through work or school, a shared, checked summary helps everyone remember what was decided.
- **For your business or work:** You can focus on the conversation and get the decisions and next steps in writing afterward, in Word or Excel if you need a document.
- **If you're just getting started:** Try one short internal meeting: turn on transcription, ask Copilot one question during the meeting, and open the Recap tab afterward.

## Try it now

Start a short test meeting with a colleague in your organization. Select **More actions** › **Transcribe**, talk for two minutes about a pretend project, and ask Copilot: "What are the next steps so far?" After the meeting, open the meeting chat, select **Recap**, and ask Copilot one more question.
